sentences.en: Modern Ukraine was entirely created by Russia.
sentences.zh: 现代乌克兰完全是由俄罗斯创造的。

sentences.en: That was Vladimir Putin in a televised address that he gave on the 21st of February.
sentences.zh: 这是弗拉基米尔·普京在2月21日发表的电视讲话中的内容。

sentences.en: And Dominic, the Russian president has really been casting himself as a top analyst of Ukrainian history recently, hasn't he?
sentences.zh: 多米尼克，这位俄罗斯总统最近真的把自己塑造成了一位乌克兰历史的顶级分析师，不是吗？

sentences.en: He has indeed, Tom.
sentences.zh: 确实如此，汤姆。

sentences.en: Obviously, we've been looking forward to doing a podcast about the history of Ukraine for a while.
sentences.zh: 显然，我们期待做一期关于乌克兰历史的播客已经有一段时间了。

sentences.en: We did think about having a self-styled historian of Ukraine,
sentences.zh: 我们确实考虑过请一位自封的乌克兰历史学家，

sentences.en: Vladimir Putin from Moscow, but he's otherwise engaged, it seems, in invading Ukraine.
sentences.zh: 也就是来自莫斯科的弗拉基米尔·普京，但他似乎正忙于入侵乌克兰，无暇他顾。

sentences.en: So we're going to do the whole sweep ourselves without his assistance, would you believe?
sentences.zh: 所以，你敢相信吗？我们要在他人的帮助下，自己完成整个历史脉络的梳理。

sentences.en: It's an amazingly interesting, convoluted and complicated story, the history of Ukraine.
sentences.zh: 乌克兰的历史是一个极其有趣、错综复杂且纠葛不断的故事。

sentences.en: It is, absolutely.
sentences.zh: 确实如此，绝对是这样。

sentences.en: And on that line that I began with, modern Ukraine was entirely created by
sentences.zh: 回到我开头提到的那句话，现代乌克兰完全是由

sentences.en: Russia.
sentences.zh: 俄罗斯创造的。

sentences.en: I mean, that is very important to Putin.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这对普京来说非常重要。

sentences.en: Obviously, it provides him with his casus belli, his justification for invading Ukraine.
sentences.zh: 显然，这为他提供了战争借口，即他入侵乌克兰的理由。

sentences.en: But implicit in our intention to look at the history of Ukraine as something distinct is a kind of rejection of that idea, isn't there?
sentences.zh: 但我们打算将乌克兰历史视为一个独立课题，这本身就隐含着对那种观点的某种排斥，不是吗？

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: I don't think, well, we're going to go through the history for, you know, 1,500 years or so,
sentences.zh: 我不认为……好吧，我们要梳理大约1500年左右的历史，

sentences.en: 1,200 years, I suppose.
sentences.zh: 我想应该是1200年。

sentences.en: But I don't think that history does show that Ukraine was created by the Bolsheviks.
sentences.zh: 但我不认为历史表明乌克兰是由布尔什维克创造的。

sentences.en: I don't think it was.
sentences.zh: 我不认为它是。

sentences.en: There's obviously Ukrainian national sensibility before that.
sentences.zh: 在此之前，显然已经存在乌克兰民族意识了。

sentences.en: A sense of Ukraine is a distinct place.
sentences.zh: 一种将乌克兰视为独立之地的意识。

sentences.en: The name Ukraine means kind of Ukraine, the land on the edge, the kind of borderland.
sentences.zh: “乌克兰”这个名字的意思有点像“边陲之地”，即边缘的土地。

sentences.en: And that's part of Ukraine's problem.
sentences.zh: 这也是乌克兰问题的一部分。

sentences.en: But it is not Muscovy.
sentences.zh: 但它不是莫斯科公国。

sentences.en: It is not Russia.
sentences.zh: 它不是俄罗斯。

sentences.en: It is something distinct.
sentences.zh: 它是某种独立的存在。

sentences.en: And to Vladimir Putin, that is an affront, because he thinks it should be part of Russia, that the Ukrainians are little Russians.
sentences.zh: 而对弗拉基米尔·普京来说，这是一种冒犯，因为他认为它应该是俄罗斯的一部分，认为乌克兰人是“小俄罗斯人”。

sentences.en: But as we shall see in the sweep, they have a very entangled, complicated history, rather like Britain and Ireland,
sentences.zh: 但正如我们将在梳理中看到的，他们有着非常纠缠、复杂的历史，就像英国和爱尔兰一样，

sentences.en: actually, or, you know, lots of other countries with smaller neighbours, but they are different phenomena.
sentences.zh: 实际上，或者说，你知道，还有许多其他拥有较小邻国的国家，但它们是不同的现象。

sentences.en: And Dominic, do you think that the reason that this story is very, very complicated, that, you know, as the listeners will find out, there are a lot of partitions, the borders kind
sentences.zh: 多米尼克，你认为这个故事之所以非常、非常复杂，是因为，你知道，正如听众们将会发现的那样，这里发生过很多次领土分割，边界有时

sentences.en: of move this way and that they vanish completely, and so on.
sentences.zh: 这样变动，有时那样变动，甚至完全消失，等等。

sentences.en: Do you think that that is essentially what enables Putin to make this case, that Ukraine often, I mean, you know, hasn't existed as a national entity for long sweeps of time?
sentences.zh: 你认为这本质上就是普京能够提出这种论点的原因吗？即乌克兰在很长一段时间内，我的意思是，你知道，并没有作为一个民族实体存在过？

sentences.en: Yeah, I think there's a lot of truth in that, Tom.
sentences.zh: 是的，我认为其中有很多道理，汤姆。

sentences.en: I think it's part of it.
sentences.zh: 我认为这是原因的一部分。

sentences.en: It's part of a part of Europe that includes, let's say, Poland, or Belarus, where borders
sentences.zh: 它是欧洲的一部分，包括波兰或白俄罗斯，那里的边界

sentences.en: have changed a lot, where empires, great empires have swallowed up nations, and then they've disgorged them again at the end.
sentences.zh: 变动很大，伟大的帝国吞并了国家，最后又把它们吐了出来。

sentences.en: And I think that makes the story much more complicated.
sentences.zh: 我认为这使得故事变得更加复杂。

sentences.en: And almost every detail of what we'll be talking about is actually contested.
sentences.zh: 而且我们谈论的几乎每一个细节实际上都是有争议的。

sentences.en: So the name, even the names, you know, you and I both call Kiev, well, we think of it as Kiev.
sentences.zh: 所以名字，甚至名字，你知道，你我都叫它“基辅”（Kiev），嗯，我们认为它是“基辅”。

sentences.en: As in chicken Kiev, don't we?
sentences.zh: 就像“基辅鸡”（chicken Kiev）那样，不是吗？

sentences.en: Exactly, because we're children of the sort of 70s.
sentences.zh: 没错，因为我们是70年代成长起来的一代人。

sentences.en: Of that age.
sentences.zh: 那个时代的人。

sentences.en: And even the names of the places, the names of the people
sentences.zh: 甚至地名、人名

sentences.en: are contested.
sentences.zh: 都是有争议的。

sentences.en: So for those of you who are listening, kind of poised to complain, we'll probably get them all wrong one way or another, because that's the nature of the beast, actually.
sentences.zh: 所以对于那些正在收听、准备抱怨的听众，我们很可能会以某种方式把它们都弄错，因为这实际上就是这类问题的本质。

sentences.en: I mean, even the very origins of Ukraine have been argued about by historians.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，甚至连乌克兰的起源都被历史学家争论不休。

sentences.en: Well, Dominic, just before we go back and we start looking at the history of it, two further questions.
sentences.zh: 好吧，多米尼克，在我们回顾并开始研究它的历史之前，还有两个问题。

sentences.en: The first is, do you think our sense of Ukraine as a distinct national cultural entity, that that's been blotted out by the fact that its history in the 20th century was so
sentences.zh: 第一个是，你认为我们对乌克兰作为一个独特的民族文化实体的认知，是否因为其20世纪的历史太过

sentences.en: horrendous, so that we tend to think of its sufferings, rather than perhaps of its cultural achievements?
sentences.zh: 惨烈而被掩盖了，以至于我们倾向于想到它的苦难，而不是它的文化成就？

sentences.en: Yeah, I think that's a really good point, Tom.
sentences.zh: 是的，我认为这是一个非常好的观点，汤姆。

sentences.en: We do think we think of Ukraine as part to what the historian Timothy Snyder calls the bloodlands.
sentences.zh: 我们确实认为乌克兰是历史学家蒂莫西·斯奈德（Timothy Snyder）所称的“血色大地”（bloodlands）的一部分。

sentences.en: So kind of Belarus, Ukraine, Lithuania,
sentences.zh: 也就是白俄罗斯、乌克兰、立陶宛、

sentences.en: Poland, places that were fought over by Hitler and Stalin, basically, is just a sort of colossal blood-soaked battleground.
sentences.zh: 波兰，这些基本上是被希特勒和斯大林争夺的地方，简直就是一个巨大的、血流成河的战场。

sentences.en: And there is much more to the history than that.
sentences.zh: 历史远不止于此。

sentences.en: But it has to be said,
sentences.zh: 但必须说的是，

sentences.en: you know, there's an awful lot of terrible suffering in Ukrainian history.
sentences.zh: 你知道，乌克兰历史上有太多可怕的苦难。

sentences.en: I mean, there's a period in the 17th century that's just called the ruin.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，17世纪有一段时期被称为“大动乱”（the ruin）。

sentences.en: And when you've got a bit of your history that's called that, you know it's not good.
sentences.zh: 当你历史的一部分被称为这个名字时，你就知道那段时期并不好过。

sentences.en: And one last question before we plunge into the vast sweep of Ukrainian history.
sentences.zh: 在我们深入探讨乌克兰历史的宏大脉络之前，最后一个问题。

sentences.en: Previously, we did a kind of emergency episode on the history of
sentences.zh: 之前，我们做过一期关于

sentences.en: Afghanistan when the American evacuation happened.
sentences.zh: 阿富汗历史的紧急播客，当时美国正在撤军。

sentences.en: So this is the second time that we're responding to great geopolitical events with a kind of emergency episode of this podcaSt. Do you, I mean,
sentences.zh: 所以这是我们第二次以这种紧急播客的形式来回应重大的地缘政治事件。你，我的意思是，

sentences.en: how large crisis do you think this is as a historian of modern Britain, modern America, modern Europe, and presumably a greater moment of geopolitical crisis than the evacuation of
sentences.zh: 作为一个现代英国、现代美国、现代欧洲的历史学家，你认为这是一场多大的危机？这大概比北约从

sentences.en: Afghanistan by NATO?
sentences.zh: 阿富汗撤军带来的地缘政治危机时刻更重大吧？

sentences.en: Yeah, I think absolutely bigger than the evacuation.
sentences.zh: 是的，我认为绝对比那次撤军要大得多。

sentences.en: The evacuation of
sentences.zh: 从

sentences.en: Afghanistan was a humiliation for the Western powers and for the Western kind of model, but it wasn't an existential threat.
sentences.zh: 阿富汗撤军对西方大国和西方模式来说是一种羞辱，但它并不是一种生存威胁。

sentences.en: I think it's no exaggeration to say it's the great crisis really that probably the world has faced since the Cuban Missile Crisis in 1962.
sentences.zh: 我认为毫不夸张地说，这大概是自1962年古巴导弹危机以来世界所面临的最大危机。

sentences.en: I mean, the comparison that a lot of people make is with the 1930s.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，很多人将其与20世纪30年代进行比较。

sentences.en: It's maybe not massively, I mean, it's obviously not quite on that scale, but you know, a war in Europe that could see tens of thousands, hundreds of thousands of people killed,
sentences.zh: 可能规模上没有那么大，我的意思是，显然没有达到那个程度，但你知道，一场可能导致成千上万、数十万人死亡的欧洲战争，

sentences.en: could see a huge capital city in Kiev be surrounded, potentially bombed.
sentences.zh: 可能看到像基辅这样的大城市被包围，甚至遭到轰炸。

sentences.en: I mean, that's a pretty terrifying prospect.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这是一个相当可怕的前景。

sentences.en: And, you know, you can see it in the, in the, in the sort of the stock market and oil prices that will have, well, even if, you know, Britain and the Western powers don't become
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，你可以从股市和油价中看出来，即使，你知道，英国和西方大国没有

sentences.en: militarily directly sucked in, it will have a huge impact, I would say, on the lives of ordinary people.
sentences.zh: 直接卷入军事冲突，我也认为这对普通人的生活将产生巨大的影响。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So the specific measure that Putin announced on in his televised speech on Monday was
sentences.zh: 所以普京在周一的电视讲话中宣布的具体措施是，

sentences.en: that he was, um, recognizing the independence and sovereignty of the Donetsk People's Republic and the Luhansk People's Republic.
sentences.zh: 他承认了“顿涅茨克人民共和国”和“卢甘斯克人民共和国”的独立和主权。

sentences.en: And these are regions in the, um, the east of Ukraine, very heavily industrialized with a lot of Russian speakers.
sentences.zh: 这些是位于乌克兰东部的地区，工业化程度很高，有很多俄语使用者。

sentences.en: Um, previously he had annexed, um, the Crimea, which had been part of Ukraine, but previously hadn't.
sentences.zh: 嗯，此前他吞并了克里米亚，克里米亚曾是乌克兰的一部分，但之前并不是。

sentences.en: I mean, and essentially the point of this is that the borders are constantly slipping in this area.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，本质上这一点说明了该地区的边界在不断变动。

sentences.en: And you could argue that that's because it has a kind of fundamentally featureless quality, the landscape, that it's very difficult to draw borders on it.
sentences.zh: 你可以争辩说，这是因为该景观具有某种根本性的平淡特征，很难在上面划定边界。

sentences.en: And do you know, Dominic, the first historian to point this out, how, how difficult and challenging it was to, to put a, to kind of
sentences.zh: 多米尼克，你知道第一位指出这一点的历史学家是谁吗？指出在这一地区游荡时，想要

sentences.en: pin down features to work out where you were, if you were roaming around this land?
sentences.zh: 确定地标以弄清自己身在何处是多么困难和具有挑战性？

sentences.en: Uh, well, since it's you, Tom, I'm going to guess it's Greek.
sentences.zh: 呃，既然是你问，汤姆，我猜是希腊人。

sentences.en: Is it Greek?
sentences.zh: 是希腊人吗？

sentences.en: Is it, um, is it the father of history?
sentences.zh: 是……是历史之父吗？

sentences.en: It is.
sentences.zh: 正是。

sentences.en: It's Herodotus.
sentences.zh: 是希罗多德。

sentences.en: So this is really, this is my, my big contribution is that, um, the land that we now call Ukraine first appears in the very first work of history ever written, which is Herodotus's
sentences.zh: 所以，我最大的贡献就是，我们现在所说的乌克兰这片土地，最早出现在有史以来第一部历史著作中，也就是希罗多德的

sentences.en: histories.
sentences.zh: 《历史》。

sentences.en: And he describes the Persian King Darius, um, trying to conquer the Scythians, the people who inhabit that region.
sentences.zh: 他描述了波斯国王大流士试图征服斯基泰人，即居住在该地区的人民。

sentences.en: And basically the Scythians just run away and poor old Darius goes kind of herring around all over the place and he just can't find anything to conquer.
sentences.zh: 基本上，斯基泰人只是逃跑了，可怜的大流士到处乱窜，却找不到任何东西可以征服。

sentences.en: Um, and then he, he withdraws and, uh, he abandons Ukraine to the, uh, the kind of the various nomadic people who had lived there.
sentences.zh: 嗯，然后他撤退了，他把乌克兰留给了居住在那里的各种游牧民族。

sentences.en: And essentially that is its history for another, um, well, certainly another thousand years, thousand years
sentences.zh: 本质上，这就是它此后又一个，嗯，至少又一个一千年，一千年

sentences.en: and more is various nomadic peoples occupying it kind of loose, vague empires.
sentences.zh: 多的历史，各种游牧民族占据着它，形成某种松散、模糊的帝国。

sentences.en: So Dominic, we actually did, um, uh, quite recently about a month ago, an episode on, um, the Vikings in the East about how,
sentences.zh: 多米尼克，我们实际上在不久前，大约一个月前，做过一期关于东方维京人的节目，讲述了

sentences.en: um, Scandinavians came down the Nipa, uh, and, and, and established a great capital at Kiev.
sentences.zh: 斯堪的纳维亚人如何顺着第聂伯河而下，并在基辅建立了伟大的首都。

sentences.en: Um, but you remember, you remember that we had the, uh, the Ferocious Pechenegs who were.
sentences.zh: 嗯，但你还记得吗，你记得我们提到过凶猛的佩切涅格人吗？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 记得。

sentences.en: The Pechenegs were very fierce.
sentences.zh: 佩切涅格人非常凶猛。

sentences.en: Very fierce.
sentences.zh: 非常凶猛。

sentences.en: They were cutting off people's heads and turning them into, into, into golden drinking vessels.
sentences.zh: 他们砍下人们的头颅，把它们做成金色的饮酒器皿。

sentences.en: All that kind of stuff.
sentences.zh: 诸如此类的事情。

sentences.en: That was, that was absolutely par for the course.
sentences.zh: 那在当时绝对是司空见惯的。

sentences.en: Which the Scythians had been doing back in, uh, back in Herodotus' day.
sentences.zh: 这正是斯基泰人在希罗多德时代所做的事情。

sentences.en: So it was just a thing that people say about nomads, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 所以这只是人们对游牧民族的刻板印象，不是吗？

sentences.en: It's just the sort of standard thing that people say.
sentences.zh: 这只是人们说的标准套话。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So we did do the Vikings in the East podcast and that's where the Ukrainian history and indeed, I mean, this is how complicated it is.
sentences.zh: 所以我们做了关于东方维京人的播客，而乌克兰历史，实际上，我的意思是，这正是它复杂的地方，

sentences.en: And indeed Russian history often begins.
sentences.zh: 确实，俄罗斯历史往往也从这里开始。

sentences.en: So it begins with, for those people who didn't listen to those Viking episodes, um, the Vikings
sentences.zh: 所以对于那些没有听过那些维京人节目的听众来说，它始于维京人，

sentences.en: before they came, actually pretty much just before they came West to England and battled,
sentences.zh: 在他们来到这里之前，实际上就在他们向西前往英格兰并与盎格鲁-撒克逊人作战之前，

sentences.en: you know, the Anglo-Saxons now for the great, they went East and they went down the rivers, down the Dnieper and the Volga.
sentences.zh: 他们向东进发，顺着河流，沿着第聂伯河和伏尔加河而下。

sentences.en: And they, this fellow called Rurik legend has it, was asked to come into Novgorod by the local Slavs and basically sort it all out and install sort of,
sentences.zh: 传说一个叫留里克的人被当地的斯拉夫人邀请到诺夫哥罗德，基本上是去解决所有问题，并建立一种，

sentences.en: uh, sort of, uh, the, the, the firm smack of government.
sentences.zh: 呃，一种强有力的政府统治。

sentences.en: And, um, then some pals of his or some sort of cronies, Askold and Deer, they went off and founded Kiev.
sentences.zh: 然后他的一些伙伴或亲信，阿斯科尔德和迪尔，他们离开并建立了基辅。

sentences.en: And then one of Rurik's, another sort of crony of his, who was, who was the sort of regent for Rurik's son, Igor, a man called Oleg.
sentences.zh: 然后留里克的另一个亲信，也就是留里克儿子伊戈尔的摄政王，一个叫奥列格的人，

sentences.en: He went and captured Kiev.
sentences.zh: 他去占领了基辅。

sentences.en: And basically that, that sort of bit of Viking feuding started this state, which you know a lot about Tom, which is Kievan Rus.
sentences.zh: 基本上，那段维京人的纷争开启了这个国家，也就是你很了解的，汤姆，基辅罗斯。

sentences.en: And that's where we get Russia, the word Russia from.
sentences.zh: 这就是我们得到“俄罗斯”这个词的由来。

sentences.en: Yeah, but it's ruled from Kiev.
sentences.zh: 是的，但它是从基辅统治的。

sentences.en: Um, so Kiev, which I think had actually existed before they arrive.
sentences.zh: 嗯，所以基辅，我想在他们到达之前其实就已经存在了。

sentences.en: It's been a kind of Slav town, hadn't it?
sentences.zh: 它一直是一个斯拉夫城镇，不是吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, it kind of fought on a hill.
